stimuli.text: Researchers investigated whether agreeing to a small request makes people more likely to agree to a large one. They recruited 120 homeowners and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Homeowners in one condition were first asked to sign a road-safety petition and two weeks later were asked to put a large sign in their garden. Homeowners in the other condition were only asked to put the large sign in their garden. The researchers then recorded the percentage of homeowners in each group who agreed to display the sign.

Researchers collected data from 350 adults. For each one, they recorded the number of stressful life events in the past year and the number of colds in the past year. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.33.

Researchers investigated whether spreading study sessions out improves long-term retention. They recruited 90 high school students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition studied a list of 40 words in six ten-minute sessions on six different days. Participants in the other condition studied the same list in a single sixty-minute session. The researchers then recorded the number of words out of 40 that each participant recalled on a test one month later.

Researchers investigated whether a new drug reduces anxiety. They recruited 150 adults diagnosed with generalized anxiety disorder and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition took the new drug every day for eight weeks. Participants in the other condition took a placebo pill that looked identical every day for eight weeks. The researchers then recorded each participant's score on a standard anxiety questionnaire after eight weeks. The results are shown in the table. The difference between the two groups had a p value of 0.41.

rows.group: The group that took the new drug
The group that took the placebo

stimuli.text: Researchers investigated whether the wording of a question changes what witnesses remember. They recruited 100 adult volunteers who watched a film of a car accident and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition were asked how fast the cars were going when they smashed into each other. Participants in the other condition were asked how fast the cars were going when they contacted each other. The researchers then recorded the speed in kilometers per hour that each participant wrote down.

Researchers investigated whether nausea after a new taste produces an aversion to that taste. They recruited 40 laboratory rats and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Rats in one condition drank sweetened water and were then given an injection that causes mild nausea. Rats in the other condition drank sweetened water and were then given a harmless salt-water injection. The researchers then recorded the volume in milliliters of sweetened water that each rat drank the next day.

Researchers collected data from 1,000 students. For each one, they recorded intelligence test score at age 11 and average school grade at age 16. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.60.
Researchers collected data from 450 adults. For each one, they recorded optimism score and the number of days of illness in a year. The correlation between the two measures was r = −0.30.

Researchers investigated whether a night without sleep slows reaction time. They recruited 60 adult volunteers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition stayed awake all night in the laboratory. Participants in the other condition slept for eight hours in the laboratory. The researchers then recorded the average time in milliseconds that each participant took to press a button when a light appeared.
Researchers collected data from 500 adults aged 20 to 80. For each one, they recorded age and score on a timed reasoning test. The correlation between the two measures was r = −0.55.
Researchers collected data from 250 adults. For each one, they recorded resting heart rate and self-rated anxiety. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.38.

Researchers investigated whether keeping a gratitude journal raises well-being. They recruited 110 adult volunteers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition wrote down three things they were grateful for every night for a month. Participants in the other condition wrote down three things they had done every night for a month. The researchers then recorded each participant's rating of life satisfaction on a scale from 1 to 10 at the end of the month.

Researchers investigated whether children imitate aggressive behavior that they observe. They recruited 72 preschool children and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition watched a video of an adult hitting an inflatable doll. Children in the other condition watched a video of an adult playing quietly with other toys. The researchers then recorded the number of times that each child hit the doll during ten minutes of free play.

Read the summary of a hypothetical study, then answer parts A to F.

**Introduction.** Researchers investigated whether caffeine improves attention. They hypothesized that caffeine would affect attention.

**Participants.** The sample was 80 university students, recruited from one city. All participants gave informed consent, were told they could withdraw at any time, and were debriefed afterward. The plan was approved by an institutional review board.

**Method.** The participants were randomly assigned to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition drank coffee containing 200 milligrams of caffeine. Participants in the other condition drank decaffeinated coffee that tasted the same. The researchers recorded the number of targets that each participant correctly detected in a ten-minute computer task.

**Results.** The group that drank caffeinated coffee: mean targets detected = 46. The group that drank decaffeinated coffee: mean targets detected = 39. The difference was statistically significant (p = 0.01).

Use the three hypothetical sources to answer the question: **Does sleep improve memory?**

**Source A.** In an experiment, 60 students learned a list of word pairs at 9 p.m. Half were randomly assigned to sleep normally and half to stay awake all night. Twelve hours later, the sleep group recalled a mean of 31 pairs out of 40 and the awake group recalled a mean of 22 (p = 0.01).

**Source B.** Researchers recorded the brain activity of 25 adults in a sleep laboratory after they had learned a maze. The more slow-wave (NREM stage 3) sleep a participant had, the faster that participant completed the maze the next morning (r = +0.55).

**Source C.** A survey of 900 high school students found that those who reported sleeping fewer than six hours on school nights had lower average grades than those who slept eight hours or more. The researchers noted that students who slept less also reported more stress and more hours of paid work.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the tendency of participants to answer in a way that makes them look good?

options.why: Self-report bias is the inaccuracy that arises when people describe their own behavior or feelings.
Experimenter bias is the influence of a researcher's expectations on the results of a study.
Correct. Social desirability bias is the tendency of participants to answer in a way that makes them look good.
Hindsight bias is the tendency, after learning an outcome, to believe one would have predicted it.

questions.explanation: Social desirability bias is the tendency of participants to answer in a way that makes them look good.

questions.stem: Neither the participants nor the assistants who recorded the results knew which condition each participant was in. What is this procedure called?

options.why: Random sampling is how participants are chosen from a population.
In a single-blind procedure only the participants are unaware.
Correct. Keeping both participants and researchers unaware of the conditions reduces bias from expectations.
That is a therapy technique, not a research control.

questions.explanation: Keeping both participants and researchers unaware of the conditions reduces bias from expectations.

questions.stem: Although he is bright and works hard, ten-year-old Theo reads far below the level expected for his age. Which disorder does this suggest?

options.why: Anorexia nervosa is the eating disorder in which a person restricts food to the point of being dangerously underweight, with an intense fear of gaining weight.
Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder is the neurodevelopmental disorder marked by inattention, hyperactivity and impulsiveness.
Correct. A specific learning disorder is the neurodevelopmental disorder marked by persistent difficulty in reading, writing or math despite normal intelligence.
Binge-eating disorder is the eating disorder in which a person repeatedly eats very large amounts and feels distress, without purging afterward.

questions.explanation: A specific learning disorder is the neurodevelopmental disorder marked by persistent difficulty in reading, writing or math despite normal intelligence.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the sunk-cost fallacy?

options.text: The way the wording of an issue affects decisions and judgments
options.why: That describes framing.

options.text: The judging of how likely something is by how well it matches a prototype, while ignoring base rates
options.why: That describes the representativeness heuristic.

options.text: The tendency to keep investing in something because of what has already been spent on it
options.why: Correct. This is what the sunk-cost fallacy means.

options.text: The judging of how likely something is by how easily examples come to mind
options.why: That describes the availability heuristic.

questions.explanation: The sunk-cost fallacy is the tendency to keep investing in something because of what has already been spent on it.

questions.stem: People who take a personality test in March get almost the same scores when they take it again in May. Which quality does the test have?

options.why: Construct validity is the extent to which a test measures the concept it claims to measure.
Correct. Test-retest reliability is the consistency of scores when the same people take the same test twice.
Predictive validity is the extent to which test scores forecast the future performance they are meant to predict.
Split-half reliability is the consistency of scores between two halves of the same test.

questions.explanation: Test-retest reliability is the consistency of scores when the same people take the same test twice.

questions.stem: A second study of a different pair of measures finds r = −0.53. Which relationship is stronger?

options.text: The relationship with the positive sign, whatever its size
options.why: The sign shows direction, not strength.

options.text: The relationship in the second study, because its coefficient is farther from zero
options.why: Correct. The strength of a correlation is its distance from zero, whatever the sign.

options.text: The relationship in the first study, because its coefficient is closer to zero
options.why: A coefficient closer to zero shows a weaker relationship.

options.text: Neither, because relationships with different signs cannot be compared
options.why: Strength can be compared by distance from zero.

questions.explanation: The strength of a correlation is its distance from zero, whatever the sign.

questions.stem: All of the subjects in this study were drawn from one group: 90 high school students. What does this most limit?

options.text: Whether the dependent variable was operationally defined
options.why: The measure was clearly defined.

options.text: How far the findings can be generalized to other populations
options.why: Correct. A sample that does not represent the wider population limits generalizability.

options.text: Whether a cause-and-effect conclusion can be drawn
options.why: Random assignment, not the sample, allows the causal conclusion.

options.text: Whether the study had a control group
options.why: The study had a comparison condition.

questions.explanation: A sample that does not represent the wider population limits generalizability.

questions.stem: Kim knows that Paris is the capital of France, although she cannot remember when she learned it. Which kind of memory is this?

options.why: Prospective memory is the memory to carry out a planned action in the future.
Correct. Semantic memory is the explicit memory of facts and general knowledge.
Episodic memory is the explicit memory of personally experienced events.
Procedural memory is the implicit memory of how to perform skills and actions.

questions.explanation: Semantic memory is the explicit memory of facts and general knowledge.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes disorganized attachment?

options.text: The insecure attachment style in which a child is very upset by separation and is not easily comforted on reunion
options.why: That describes anxious attachment.

options.text: The insecure attachment style in which a child shows confused, contradictory behavior toward the caregiver
options.why: Correct. This is what disorganized attachment means.

options.text: The insecure attachment style in which a child seems indifferent when the caregiver leaves and ignores the caregiver on return
options.why: That describes avoidant attachment.

options.text: The attachment style in which a child uses the caregiver as a safe base, is upset when the caregiver leaves and is comforted on return
options.why: That describes secure attachment.

questions.explanation: Disorganized attachment is the insecure attachment style in which a child shows confused, contradictory behavior toward the caregiver.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes an internal locus of control?

options.text: The belief that outcomes are decided by luck, fate or other people
options.why: That describes an external locus of control.

options.text: The belief that a person controls their own outcomes through their own actions
options.why: Correct. This is what an internal locus of control means.

options.text: The tendency to like something more simply because we have encountered it repeatedly
options.why: That describes the mere exposure effect.

options.text: An expectation that leads a person to act in ways that make the expectation come true
options.why: That describes a self-fulfilling prophecy.

questions.explanation: An internal locus of control is the belief that a person controls their own outcomes through their own actions.

questions.stem: Two students have racing hearts before a speech; one labels the feeling as excitement and the other as fear. The difference in their emotions is due to which of the following?

options.why: The facial-feedback hypothesis is the idea that the expression on a person's face can influence the emotion the person feels.
Correct. Cognitive appraisal is the interpretation of a situation, which shapes the emotion a person feels.
A display rule is a cultural rule about which emotions may be shown, when and to whom.
Universal emotions is the basic emotions, such as happiness, sadness, fear and anger, whose facial expressions are recognized across cultures.

questions.explanation: Cognitive appraisal is the interpretation of a situation, which shapes the emotion a person feels.

questions.stem: Mia's parents are loving but let her stay up as late as she likes and rarely enforce any rules. Which parenting style is this?

options.why: Correct. Permissive parenting is the parenting style that makes few demands and sets few limits.
Authoritarian parenting is the parenting style that sets strict rules and expects obedience, with little warmth or discussion.
Temperament is a person's characteristic emotional reactivity and intensity, which appears early in life.
Authoritative parenting is the parenting style that sets firm rules but explains them, listens and is warm.

questions.explanation: Permissive parenting is the parenting style that makes few demands and sets few limits.

questions.stem: A therapist asks a client to explain what her symptoms mean in her culture rather than assuming he already knows. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Deinstitutionalization is the movement, begun in the 1950s, of patients out of psychiatric hospitals and into community care.
Evidence-based practice is the choosing of treatments on the basis of research, clinical skill and the client's own values.
Correct. Cultural humility is a therapist's openness to learning about a client's culture and awareness of the limits of their own view.
The therapeutic alliance is the bond of trust and cooperation between therapist and client.

questions.explanation: Cultural humility is a therapist's openness to learning about a client's culture and awareness of the limits of their own view.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the desire to do something for its own sake, because it is enjoyable or satisfying?

options.why: Extrinsic motivation is the desire to do something to gain a reward or avoid a punishment.
Correct. Intrinsic motivation is the desire to do something for its own sake, because it is enjoyable or satisfying.
An avoidance-avoidance conflict is a conflict in which a person must choose between two unattractive options.
An approach-approach conflict is a conflict in which a person must choose between two attractive options.

questions.explanation: Intrinsic motivation is the desire to do something for its own sake, because it is enjoyable or satisfying.

questions.stem: Dee cannot stop thinking that her hands are covered in germs. This repeated, unwanted thought is which of the following?

options.why: A compulsion is a repeated action that a person feels driven to perform to reduce anxiety.
Hoarding disorder is the disorder in which a person cannot throw away possessions, so that living spaces become cluttered.
Correct. An obsession is an unwanted thought or urge that keeps returning and causes anxiety.
Dissociative identity disorder is the disorder in which a person shows two or more distinct personalities that take control at different times.

questions.explanation: An obsession is an unwanted thought or urge that keeps returning and causes anxiety.

questions.stem: A client with borderline personality disorder learns mindfulness, ways of tolerating distress and ways of regulating emotions. Which therapy is this?

options.why: Cognitive-behavioral therapy is the therapy that combines changing self-defeating thoughts with changing behavior.
The cognitive triad is the pattern of negative thoughts about oneself, the world and the future that is found in depression.
Correct. Dialectical behavior therapy is the therapy that teaches skills for tolerating distress and controlling emotions, often used for borderline personality disorder.
Rational emotive behavior therapy is the confrontational cognitive therapy, developed by Ellis, that actively challenges a client's irrational beliefs.

questions.explanation: Dialectical behavior therapy is the therapy that teaches skills for tolerating distress and controlling emotions, often used for borderline personality disorder.

questions.stem: A shy teenager avoids parties, so she gets little social practice, which makes her even more shy. This interaction between thoughts, behavior and environment is called which of the following?

options.why: Self-concept is all the thoughts and feelings a person has in answer to the question 'Who am I?'.
Self-esteem is a person's overall feeling of self-worth.
Correct. Reciprocal determinism is the idea that a person's behavior, thoughts and environment all influence one another.
Factor analysis is the statistical method that finds clusters of related test items, used to identify basic traits.

questions.explanation: Reciprocal determinism is the idea that a person's behavior, thoughts and environment all influence one another.

questions.stem: A fifteen-year-old debates what would happen to society if people could live forever. Which of Piaget's stages allows this hypothetical thinking?

options.why: The concrete operational stage is Piaget's stage from about age 7 to 11, in which children think logically about real objects and events.
The sensorimotor stage is Piaget's stage from birth to about age 2, in which infants know the world through senses and actions.
Correct. The formal operational stage is Piaget's stage from about age 12 on, in which people can reason about abstract and hypothetical ideas.
The preoperational stage is Piaget's stage from about age 2 to 7, in which children use words and images but cannot yet reason logically.

questions.explanation: The formal operational stage is Piaget's stage from about age 12 on, in which people can reason about abstract and hypothetical ideas.

questions.stem: Knowing that adding '-ed' to 'laugh' means the action happened in the past is part of which of the following?

options.why: Grammar is the whole system of rules in a language that lets people communicate.
A phoneme is the smallest distinctive unit of sound in a language.
Syntax is the rules for ordering words into sentences.
Correct. Semantics is the rules by which we get meaning from words and sentences.

questions.explanation: Semantics is the rules by which we get meaning from words and sentences.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes thrill and adventure seeking?

options.text: The form of sensation seeking that involves a loss of self-restraint, as at wild parties
options.why: That describes disinhibition.

options.text: The form of sensation seeking that involves a strong dislike of repetition and routine
options.why: That describes boredom susceptibility.

options.text: The form of sensation seeking that involves a desire for risky physical activities
options.why: Correct. This is what thrill and adventure seeking means.

options.text: The form of sensation seeking that involves a desire for new experiences through travel, art and unusual lifestyles
options.why: That describes experience seeking.

questions.explanation: Thrill and adventure seeking is the form of sensation seeking that involves a desire for risky physical activities.

questions.stem: Which statement about the results is best supported?

options.text: The difference between the groups is not statistically significant, so it could easily be due to chance
options.why: Correct. A p value above 0.05 means a difference this size would often occur by chance alone.

options.text: The difference between the groups is statistically significant
options.why: A p value of 0.41 is far above 0.05.

options.text: The independent variable had a large effect
options.why: The averages are close and the difference is not significant.

options.text: The study shows that the two conditions always give identical results
options.why: A non-significant result does not show that there is no effect at all.

questions.explanation: A p value above 0.05 means a difference this size would often occur by chance alone.

questions.stem: Which group served as the control group?

options.text: The group asked the question with the word 'contacted'
options.why: Correct. The control group is the comparison group that does not receive the treatment being tested.

options.text: The group asked the question with the word 'smashed'
options.why: This group received the treatment being tested: it is the experimental group.

options.text: Neither group, because the study had no comparison condition
options.why: The second condition is the comparison.
Only the comparison group is the control group.

questions.explanation: The control group is the comparison group that does not receive the treatment being tested.

questions.stem: Why did the researchers assign the animals to the two conditions at random?

options.text: So that nobody would know the hypothesis
options.why: That describes a blind procedure.

options.text: So that the study would have more participants
options.why: Random assignment does not change the sample size.

options.text: So that the results could be generalized to the whole population
options.why: That is the purpose of random sampling, not random assignment.

options.text: So that the two groups would be similar at the start, and any difference could be attributed to the independent variable
options.why: Correct. Random assignment spreads individual differences evenly across the conditions.

questions.explanation: Random assignment spreads individual differences evenly across the conditions.

questions.stem: After failing a quiz, Ty says, 'I am just not a math person,' and stops trying. Which belief does this show?

options.why: Stereotype lift is the boost in performance that comes from awareness that another group is negatively stereotyped.
An achievement test is a test that measures what a person has already learned.
Correct. A fixed mindset is the belief that intelligence is set and cannot be changed.
An aptitude test is a test that predicts a person's ability to learn or perform in the future.

questions.explanation: A fixed mindset is the belief that intelligence is set and cannot be changed.

questions.stem: Can the researchers conclude that intelligence test score at age 11 causes a change in average school grade at age 16?

options.text: No, because correlations can only be calculated in experiments
options.why: Correlations are calculated in non-experimental studies.

options.text: No, because a correlation does not show cause and effect
options.why: Correct. Without manipulating a variable and assigning subjects at random, other explanations cannot be ruled out.

options.text: Yes, because the sample was large
options.why: A large sample does not turn a correlation into evidence of causation.

options.text: Yes, because the correlation is not zero
options.why: Any nonzero correlation still leaves the cause unknown.

questions.explanation: Without manipulating a variable and assigning subjects at random, other explanations cannot be ruled out.

questions.stem: After losing a match, Eli thinks, 'It was one bad day and the wind was against me; I will do better next week.' Which explanatory style is this?

options.why: The fundamental attribution error is the tendency, when judging other people's behavior, to overestimate personal traits and underestimate the situation.
The actor-observer bias is the tendency to explain our own behavior by the situation but other people's behavior by their traits.
The self-serving bias is the tendency to credit our successes to ourselves and blame our failures on outside factors.
Correct. An optimistic explanatory style is the habit of explaining bad events as temporary, specific and caused by outside factors.

questions.explanation: An optimistic explanatory style is the habit of explaining bad events as temporary, specific and caused by outside factors.

questions.stem: What does the correlation show?

options.why: A correlation of zero would show no relationship.

options.text: Higher values of the first measure tend to go with higher values of the second
options.why: That would be a positive correlation.

options.text: The first measure causes the second
options.why: A correlation does not show cause and effect.

options.text: Higher values of the first measure tend to go with lower values of the second
options.why: Correct. A negative correlation means the two measures tend to move in opposite directions.

questions.explanation: A negative correlation means the two measures tend to move in opposite directions.

questions.stem: A researcher sends a questionnaire about sleep habits to 2,000 adults. Which research method is this?

options.why: Correct. A survey is the research method of collecting self-reported attitudes or behaviors from a sample by asking questions.
Naturalistic observation is the research method of watching and recording behavior in its natural setting without interfering.
An experiment is the research method in which a researcher manipulates a variable and randomly assigns participants, which allows conclusions about cause and effect.
Replication is the repeating of a study with different participants to see whether the finding holds.

questions.explanation: A survey is the research method of collecting self-reported attitudes or behaviors from a sample by asking questions.

questions.stem: Antidepressants, antipsychotics and mood stabilizers all belong to which general category of treatment?

options.why: Transcranial magnetic stimulation is the treatment in which repeated magnetic pulses are applied to the surface of the brain to treat depression.
Correct. Psychotropic medication is any drug that acts on the brain to treat the symptoms of a psychological disorder.
Electroconvulsive therapy is the treatment for severe depression in which a brief electric current is passed through the brain of an anesthetized patient.
A lobotomy is the now-abandoned form of psychosurgery that cut the nerves connecting the frontal lobes to the rest of the brain.

questions.explanation: Psychotropic medication is any drug that acts on the brain to treat the symptoms of a psychological disorder.

questions.stem: Another research team repeats this study with new subjects and obtains the same result. What is this called?

options.why: That is how subjects are placed in conditions.
Correct. Replication is repeating a study to see whether the finding holds.
That is explaining the study to participants afterward.
That is an in-depth study of one individual.

questions.explanation: Replication is repeating a study to see whether the finding holds.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes deception?

options.text: The requirement that researchers keep the physical and psychological risks to participants as low as possible
options.why: That describes protection from harm.

options.text: The agreement of participants to take part after they have been told what a study involves
options.why: That describes informed consent.

options.text: The misleading of participants about the true purpose of a study, allowed only when necessary and followed by debriefing
options.why: Correct. This is what deception means.

options.text: The keeping private of participants' identities and data
options.why: That describes confidentiality.

questions.explanation: Deception is the misleading of participants about the true purpose of a study, allowed only when necessary and followed by debriefing.

questions.stem: Years of loud concerts destroyed the hair cells in Dee's cochlea. Which kind of hearing loss does she have?

options.why: Sound localization is the ability to tell where a sound comes from, using differences in timing and loudness between the two ears.
Volley theory is the theory that groups of neurons take turns firing so that together they match high sound frequencies.
Correct. Sensorineural deafness is hearing loss caused by damage to the hair cells of the cochlea or to the auditory nerve.
Place theory is the theory that we hear different pitches because different sound waves trigger different places on the cochlea's membrane.

questions.explanation: Sensorineural deafness is hearing loss caused by damage to the hair cells of the cochlea or to the auditory nerve.

questions.stem: Two classes have the same average score, but in one class the scores are tightly bunched and in the other they are widely spread. Which statistic would show this difference?

options.why: The mode is the score that occurs most often.
The median is the middle score when the scores are placed in order.
Correct. The standard deviation is the measure of how much scores vary around the mean.
The mean is the arithmetic average of a set of scores.

questions.explanation: The standard deviation is the measure of how much scores vary around the mean.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the organizing of information into broad categories divided into narrower ones?

options.why: Distributed practice is study that is spread out over several sessions.
The method of loci is the mnemonic of imagining items placed at locations along a familiar route.
Correct. A hierarchy is the organizing of information into broad categories divided into narrower ones.
Massed practice is study that is crammed into one long session.

questions.explanation: A hierarchy is the organizing of information into broad categories divided into narrower ones.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the self-actualizing tendency?

options.text: In humanistic theory, the inborn drive of people to grow and fulfill their potential
options.why: Correct. This is what the self-actualizing tendency means.

options.text: The attitude of total acceptance toward another person, whatever they say or do
options.why: That describes unconditional positive regard.

options.text: A personality test, such as an inkblot test, that asks people to interpret unclear images in order to reveal hidden feelings
options.why: That describes a projective test.

options.text: In psychodynamic theory, a method the ego uses without awareness to reduce anxiety by distorting reality
options.why: That describes a defense mechanism.

questions.explanation: The self-actualizing tendency is in humanistic theory, the inborn drive of people to grow and fulfill their potential.

questions.stem: Hours after his last meal, Ben's stomach releases a hormone that makes him feel hungry. Which hormone is this?

options.why: Oxytocin is the hormone that promotes bonding, trust and social attachment.
Melatonin is the hormone released by the pineal gland that makes a person sleepy.
Adrenaline is the hormone released by the adrenal glands that raises heart rate and energy during stress.
Correct. Ghrelin is the hormone released by an empty stomach that increases hunger.

questions.explanation: Ghrelin is the hormone released by an empty stomach that increases hunger.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes texture gradient?

options.text: The binocular depth cue based on the difference between the images in the two eyes
options.why: That describes retinal disparity.

options.text: The monocular depth cue in which surfaces look smoother and less detailed as they get farther away
options.why: Correct. This is what texture gradient means.

options.text: The monocular depth cue in which hazy objects are seen as farther away than sharp ones
options.why: That describes relative clarity.

options.text: The monocular depth cue in which parallel lines seem to meet in the distance
options.why: That describes linear perspective.

questions.explanation: Texture gradient is the monocular depth cue in which surfaces look smoother and less detailed as they get farther away.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a possible third variable that could explain the correlation?

options.text: The number of years since leaving school
options.why: Correct. A third variable could influence both measures and so produce the correlation.
This is the statistic, not a variable.
This is one of the two variables that were measured.

options.text: Score on a timed reasoning test
options.why: This is one of the two variables that were measured.

questions.explanation: A third variable could influence both measures and so produce the correlation.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the tendency to judge other cultures by the standards of one's own culture?

options.why: Discrimination is unjustified negative behavior toward a group and its members.
An implicit attitude is an attitude that a person holds without being aware of it.
Correct. Ethnocentrism is the tendency to judge other cultures by the standards of one's own culture.
The just-world phenomenon is the tendency to believe that people get what they deserve.

questions.explanation: Ethnocentrism is the tendency to judge other cultures by the standards of one's own culture.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes motor neurons?

options.text: The cells that support, nourish, insulate and protect neurons
options.why: That describes glial cells.

options.text: The neurons that carry incoming information from the sense receptors to the brain and spinal cord
options.why: That describes sensory neurons.

options.text: The neurons that carry outgoing information from the brain and spinal cord to the muscles and glands
options.why: Correct. This is what motor neurons means.

options.text: The simple automatic pathway in which the spinal cord produces a response before the brain is aware of the stimulus
options.why: That describes the reflex arc.

questions.explanation: Motor neurons is the neurons that carry outgoing information from the brain and spinal cord to the muscles and glands.

questions.stem: A day after meeting twelve new people, Joy remembers only the names of the first two she met. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: The spacing effect is the finding that study spread over time produces better long-term memory than study crammed together.
The recency effect is the tendency to remember the last items in a list well.
Correct. The primacy effect is the tendency to remember the first items in a list well.
The serial position effect is the tendency to remember the first and last items in a list better than the middle ones.

questions.explanation: The primacy effect is the tendency to remember the first items in a list well.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the stable negative charge inside a neuron when it is not firing?

options.why: The refractory period is the brief pause after a neuron fires during which it cannot fire again.
Reuptake is the process in which the sending neuron reabsorbs leftover neurotransmitters from the synapse.
Depolarization is the change in which positive ions rush into the axon and make the inside less negative.
Correct. The resting potential is the stable negative charge inside a neuron when it is not firing.

questions.explanation: The resting potential is the stable negative charge inside a neuron when it is not firing.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the disorder in which a person has full manic episodes, usually alternating with depression?

options.why: Major depressive disorder is the disorder in which a person has at least two weeks of depressed mood or loss of interest, with other symptoms such as changes in sleep and appetite.
Bipolar II disorder is the disorder in which a person alternates between depression and a milder form of mania called hypomania.
Correct. Bipolar I disorder is the disorder in which a person has full manic episodes, usually alternating with depression.
Persistent depressive disorder is the disorder in which a person has a mildly depressed mood on most days for at least two years.

questions.explanation: Bipolar I disorder is the disorder in which a person has full manic episodes, usually alternating with depression.

questions.stem: A psychologist notes that people who score high on verbal tests also tend to score high on spatial and numerical tests, and concludes that one ability underlies them all. Which idea is this?

options.why: The Flynn effect is the steady rise in average intelligence test scores over the generations.
Mental age is the level of performance typical of a certain chronological age on an intelligence test.
Multiple intelligences is the theory that people have several independent kinds of intelligence, such as musical and interpersonal.
Correct. General intelligence is the single underlying mental ability that Spearman believed affects performance on all mental tasks.

questions.explanation: General intelligence is the single underlying mental ability that Spearman believed affects performance on all mental tasks.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the belief of young children that lifeless objects have feelings and intentions?

options.why: Theory of mind is the understanding that other people have their own thoughts, beliefs and feelings.
Conservation is the understanding that quantity stays the same when shape or arrangement changes.
Object permanence is the understanding that things continue to exist when they are out of sight.
Correct. Animism is the belief of young children that lifeless objects have feelings and intentions.

questions.explanation: Animism is the belief of young children that lifeless objects have feelings and intentions.

questions.stem: A child's schooling is disrupted by a pandemic at age eight. In ecological systems theory, the timing of this event is part of which system?

options.why: The exosystem is in ecological systems theory, the settings that affect a child indirectly, such as a parent's workplace.
Correct. The chronosystem is in ecological systems theory, the life stage and historical events that affect a child.
The microsystem is in ecological systems theory, the groups that have direct contact with the child, such as family and school.
The mesosystem is in ecological systems theory, the relationships between the groups in a child's immediate surroundings.

questions.explanation: The chronosystem is in ecological systems theory, the life stage and historical events that affect a child.

questions.stem: Because of her fears, Ana can no longer hold a job or see her friends. Which criterion for a psychological disorder does this meet?

options.why: Stigma is the negative attitudes and discrimination directed at people who have a psychological disorder.
Correct. Dysfunction is the criterion for a disorder that the behavior interferes with daily life, such as work and relationships.
Distress is the criterion for a disorder that the behavior causes suffering to the person.
The ICD is the World Health Organization's international system for classifying all diseases, including mental disorders.

questions.explanation: Dysfunction is the criterion for a disorder that the behavior interferes with daily life, such as work and relationships.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the discomfort a person feels when their actions and attitudes conflict, which motivates a change in one of them?

options.why: Confirmation bias is the tendency to search for and favor information that supports what one already believes.
Correct. Cognitive dissonance is the discomfort a person feels when their actions and attitudes conflict, which motivates a change in one of them.
Belief perseverance is the tendency to hold on to a belief even after the evidence for it has been discredited.
In-group bias is the tendency to favor the members of one's own group.

questions.explanation: Cognitive dissonance is the discomfort a person feels when their actions and attitudes conflict, which motivates a change in one of them.

questions.stem: After a stroke, Mrs. Cho speaks fluently, but her sentences make no sense and she cannot understand others. Which area was most likely damaged?

options.why: Broca's area is the area in the left frontal lobe that controls speech production.
Aphasia is an impairment of language caused by brain damage.
Hemispheric specialization is the tendency for each side of the brain to handle certain functions, such as language in the left hemisphere.
Correct. Wernicke's area is the area in the left temporal lobe that controls language comprehension.

questions.explanation: Wernicke's area is the area in the left temporal lobe that controls language comprehension.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as Erikson's stage in young adulthood, in which people seek close, lasting relationships?

options.why: Identity versus role confusion is Erikson's stage in adolescence, in which teenagers work out who they are.
Correct. Intimacy versus isolation is Erikson's stage in young adulthood, in which people seek close, lasting relationships.
Integrity versus despair is Erikson's stage in late adulthood, in which people look back on life with satisfaction or regret.
Generativity versus stagnation is Erikson's stage in middle adulthood, in which people seek to contribute to the world through family and work.

questions.explanation: Intimacy versus isolation is Erikson's stage in young adulthood, in which people seek close, lasting relationships.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as a sensory experience, such as hearing voices, that occurs without any outside stimulus?

options.why: Correct. A hallucination is a sensory experience, such as hearing voices, that occurs without any outside stimulus.
A delusion is a false belief, often of persecution or grandeur, that a person holds despite clear evidence against it.
Disorganized speech is the jumbled, illogical speech, sometimes called word salad, that is a symptom of schizophrenia.
Flat affect is a lack of emotional expression in the face and voice.

questions.explanation: A hallucination is a sensory experience, such as hearing voices, that occurs without any outside stimulus.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes random sampling?

options.text: The extent to which the findings of a study apply to people beyond the sample
options.why: That describes generalizability.

options.text: A flaw in selecting participants that makes the sample unlike the population
options.why: That describes sampling bias.

options.text: A sample whose characteristics match those of the population it is drawn from
options.why: That describes a representative sample.

options.text: The selecting of participants so that every member of the population has an equal chance of being chosen
options.why: Correct. This is what random sampling means.

questions.explanation: Random sampling is the selecting of participants so that every member of the population has an equal chance of being chosen.

questions.stem: Can the researchers conclude that resting heart rate causes a change in self-rated anxiety?

options.text: No, because correlations can only be calculated in experiments
options.why: Correlations are calculated in non-experimental studies.

options.text: No, because a correlation does not show cause and effect
options.why: Correct. Without manipulating a variable and assigning subjects at random, other explanations cannot be ruled out.

options.text: Yes, because the correlation is not zero
options.why: Any nonzero correlation still leaves the cause unknown.

options.text: Yes, because the sample was large
options.why: A large sample does not turn a correlation into evidence of causation.

questions.explanation: Without manipulating a variable and assigning subjects at random, other explanations cannot be ruled out.

questions.stem: Why did the researchers assign the participants to the two conditions at random?

options.text: So that the results could be generalized to the whole population
options.why: That is the purpose of random sampling, not random assignment.

options.text: So that nobody would know the hypothesis
options.why: That describes a blind procedure.

options.text: So that the study would have more participants
options.why: Random assignment does not change the sample size.

options.text: So that the two groups would be similar at the start, and any difference could be attributed to the independent variable
options.why: Correct. Random assignment spreads individual differences evenly across the conditions.

questions.explanation: Random assignment spreads individual differences evenly across the conditions.

questions.stem: Ice cream sales and drownings rise together, but both are caused by hot weather. Which problem does this illustrate?

options.why: The directionality problem is the difficulty in a correlational study of knowing which variable influences the other.
The correlation coefficient is the number from −1.00 to +1.00 that shows the direction and strength of a relationship.
A negative correlation is a relationship in which one variable rises as the other falls.
Correct. The third variable problem is the possibility that an unmeasured factor causes the relationship between two correlated variables.

questions.explanation: The third variable problem is the possibility that an unmeasured factor causes the relationship between two correlated variables.

questions.stem: Neurotransmitters must cross a small space to reach the next neuron. What is this space called?

options.why: The cell body is the part of the neuron that contains the nucleus and keeps the cell alive.
Correct. The synapse is the tiny gap between the sending neuron and the receiving neuron.
The myelin sheath is the fatty layer around some axons that speeds up neural impulses.
The axon is the long fiber that carries the neural impulse away from the cell body toward other cells.

questions.explanation: The synapse is the tiny gap between the sending neuron and the receiving neuron.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes sublimation?

options.text: The defense mechanism of retreating to behavior from an earlier stage of development
options.why: That describes regression.

options.text: The defense mechanism of acting in the opposite way to one's unacceptable impulses
options.why: That describes reaction formation.

options.text: The defense mechanism of turning unacceptable impulses into socially valued activities
options.why: Correct. This is what sublimation means.

options.text: The defense mechanism of pushing anxiety-arousing thoughts and memories out of awareness
options.why: That describes repression.

questions.explanation: Sublimation is the defense mechanism of turning unacceptable impulses into socially valued activities.

questions.stem: Positive psychologists group teamwork, fairness and leadership under which virtue?

options.why: Transcendence is the category of character strengths that includes gratitude, hope, humor and appreciation of beauty.
Wisdom is the category of character strengths that includes creativity, curiosity and love of learning.
Humanity is the category of character strengths that includes love, kindness and social intelligence.
Correct. Justice is the category of character strengths that includes teamwork, fairness and leadership.

questions.explanation: Justice is the category of character strengths that includes teamwork, fairness and leadership.

questions.stem: As well as obtaining permission from the parents, the researchers asked each child whether he or she was willing to take part. What is the child's agreement called?

options.why: Confidentiality is keeping data private.
Deception is misleading participants about the study.
Correct. Minors cannot give legal consent, so they give assent and their parents give consent.
Debriefing happens after the study.

questions.explanation: Minors cannot give legal consent, so they give assent and their parents give consent.

questions.stem: Students catch more colds during exam weeks than at other times of year. Which effect of stress best explains this?

options.why: Correct. Immune suppression is the weakening of the body's defenses against illness during long-term stress.
Emotion-focused coping is the reducing of stress by managing one's emotional reaction rather than the stressor.
Problem-focused coping is the reducing of stress by changing the stressor itself or the way one deals with it.
Hypertension is persistently high blood pressure, which is made more likely by chronic stress.

questions.explanation: Immune suppression is the weakening of the body's defenses against illness during long-term stress.

questions.stem: A diagram labels every nerve that lies outside the brain and spinal cord. Which part of the nervous system does the diagram show?

options.why: Correct. The peripheral nervous system is the sensory and motor nerves that connect the brain and spinal cord to the rest of the body.
The central nervous system is the brain and spinal cord.
The autonomic nervous system is the division of the peripheral nervous system that controls glands and internal organs without conscious effort.
The sympathetic nervous system is the division of the autonomic nervous system that arouses the body for fight or flight.

questions.explanation: The peripheral nervous system is the sensory and motor nerves that connect the brain and spinal cord to the rest of the body.

questions.stem: Even in a room with no clocks or windows, volunteers still become sleepy and alert on a cycle of about a day. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: NREM stage 3 is the deep sleep stage marked by slow delta waves, in which a person is hard to wake.
Correct. The circadian rhythm is the body's roughly 24-hour cycle of wakefulness and sleep.
REM rebound is the tendency to have more REM sleep after being deprived of it.
NREM stage 1 is the brief, light first stage of sleep, in which a person may have hypnagogic sensations such as falling.

questions.explanation: The circadian rhythm is the body's roughly 24-hour cycle of wakefulness and sleep.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes biological preparedness?

options.text: The decrease in response to a stimulus that is presented over and over
options.why: That describes habituation.

options.text: A learned dislike of a food that was followed by illness
options.why: That describes a taste aversion.

options.text: The inborn readiness to learn some associations, such as taste and nausea, more easily than others
options.why: Correct. This is what biological preparedness means.

options.text: Learning that happens after a single pairing of two stimuli
options.why: That describes one-trial conditioning.

questions.explanation: Biological preparedness is the inborn readiness to learn some associations, such as taste and nausea, more easily than others.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the conditioned stimulus?

options.text: In classical conditioning, the natural, unlearned response to a stimulus
options.why: That describes the unconditioned response.

options.text: In classical conditioning, the originally neutral stimulus that triggers a response after being paired with another stimulus
options.why: Correct. This is what the conditioned stimulus means.

options.text: In classical conditioning, the stimulus that triggers a response naturally, without learning
options.why: That describes the unconditioned stimulus.

options.text: In classical conditioning, the learned response to a previously neutral stimulus
options.why: That describes the conditioned response.

questions.explanation: The conditioned stimulus is in classical conditioning, the originally neutral stimulus that triggers a response after being paired with another stimulus.

questions.stem: Witnesses asked how fast the cars were going when they 'smashed' into each other later remember broken glass that was not there. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Correct. The misinformation effect is the distortion of a memory by misleading information received after the event.
Constructive memory is the building of a memory at retrieval from stored pieces, expectations and later information.
Imagination inflation is the increased confidence that an event happened after repeatedly imagining it.
Source amnesia is the inability to remember where, when or how a piece of information was learned.

questions.explanation: The misinformation effect is the distortion of a memory by misleading information received after the event.

questions.stem: A cake needs exactly thirty minutes in the oven, and the baker checks it more and more often as the half hour ends. Which schedule of reinforcement is this?

options.why: Correct. A fixed-interval schedule is the schedule in which the first response after a set amount of time is reinforced.
Continuous reinforcement is the schedule in which the behavior is reinforced every time it occurs.
A variable-interval schedule is the schedule in which the first response after an unpredictable amount of time is reinforced.
A fixed-ratio schedule is the schedule in which the behavior is reinforced after a set number of responses.

questions.explanation: A fixed-interval schedule is the schedule in which the first response after a set amount of time is reinforced.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the resistance phase?

options.text: The third phase of the general adaptation syndrome, in which the body's resources run out and illness becomes more likely
options.why: That describes the exhaustion phase.

options.text: Selye's three-phase description of the body's response to long-term stress: alarm, resistance and exhaustion
options.why: That describes the general adaptation syndrome.

options.text: The first phase of the general adaptation syndrome, in which the sympathetic nervous system is suddenly activated
options.why: That describes the alarm reaction.

options.text: The second phase of the general adaptation syndrome, in which the body stays highly aroused to cope with a continuing stressor
options.why: Correct. This is what the resistance phase means.

questions.explanation: The resistance phase is the second phase of the general adaptation syndrome, in which the body stays highly aroused to cope with a continuing stressor.

questions.stem: Identical twins raised apart develop different accents, diets and hobbies that match their adoptive families. This finding most supports the influence of which of the following?

options.why: A twin study is research that compares identical and fraternal twins to estimate the influence of heredity.
An adoption study is research that compares adopted children with their biological and adoptive relatives.
Eugenics is the discredited movement that misused ideas about heredity to argue for selective breeding of humans.
Correct. Nurture is the influence of environmental factors, such as upbringing and experience, on behavior and mental processes.

questions.explanation: Nurture is the influence of environmental factors, such as upbringing and experience, on behavior and mental processes.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes obedience?

options.text: The cultural pattern that gives priority to personal goals and defines identity by personal traits
options.why: That describes individualism.

options.text: The adjusting of behavior or thinking to match a group standard
options.why: That describes conformity.

options.text: The following of the direct commands of an authority figure
options.why: Correct. This is what obedience means.

options.text: A shared goal that can be reached only if groups cooperate, which reduces conflict between them
options.why: That describes a superordinate goal.

questions.explanation: Obedience is the following of the direct commands of an authority figure.

questions.stem: A clinician explains a patient's depression by her family history, her negative thinking style and her recent job loss together. Which model is this?

options.why: An eclectic approach is the use of techniques from several types of therapy, depending on the client's problem.
The diathesis-stress model is the view that a disorder develops when an inherited vulnerability is triggered by stressful experience.
Comorbidity is the presence of two or more disorders in the same person at the same time.
Correct. The biopsychosocial model is the view that disorders result from the interaction of biological, psychological and social factors.

questions.explanation: The biopsychosocial model is the view that disorders result from the interaction of biological, psychological and social factors.

questions.stem: A person sees the world entirely in shades of gray because only one type of cone, or none, works. Which condition is this?

options.why: Prosopagnosia is the inability to recognize faces, even familiar ones, after brain damage.
The trichromatic theory is the theory that the retina has three types of color receptors, sensitive to red, green and blue.
Correct. Monochromatism is a rare form of color blindness in which a person sees only shades of gray.
The opponent-process theory is the theory that color is processed in opposing pairs: red–green, blue–yellow and black–white.

questions.explanation: Monochromatism is a rare form of color blindness in which a person sees only shades of gray.

questions.stem: A man giving directions does not notice that the stranger he is talking to was swapped for a different person when a door passed between them. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Bottom-up processing is perception that starts with the raw sensory input and builds up to a complete picture.
Selective attention is the focusing of awareness on one stimulus while ignoring others.
Correct. Change blindness is the failure to notice that something in the environment has changed.
Top-down processing is perception that is guided by experience, expectations and context.

questions.explanation: Change blindness is the failure to notice that something in the environment has changed.

questions.stem: During deep sleep, the body releases growth hormone and repairs muscle tissue. This best supports which function of sleep?

options.why: Memory consolidation is the strengthening of memories that takes place during sleep.
Correct. Restoration is the repair of body and brain tissue that takes place during sleep.
The consolidation theory is the theory that dreaming helps sort and strengthen the day's memories.
The activation-synthesis theory is the theory that dreams are the brain's attempt to make sense of random neural activity during sleep.

questions.explanation: Restoration is the repair of body and brain tissue that takes place during sleep.

questions.stem: A small dot disappears when its image falls on the place where the optic nerve leaves the retina. What is this place called?

options.why: Rods is the receptor cells that detect black, white and gray and work in dim light and peripheral vision.
Correct. The blind spot is the point where the optic nerve leaves the eye, which has no receptor cells.
The fovea is the central point of the retina, where cones are packed most densely and vision is sharpest.
The retina is the light-sensitive inner surface at the back of the eye that contains the receptor cells.

questions.explanation: The blind spot is the point where the optic nerve leaves the eye, which has no receptor cells.

questions.stem: Scores on a test are normally distributed with a mean of 500 and a standard deviation of 20. About what percentage of scores are above 500?

options.why: This does not match the 68–95 rule for a normal distribution.
This does not match the 68–95 rule for a normal distribution.
Correct. A normal distribution is symmetrical, so half the scores lie above the mean.
This does not match the 68–95 rule for a normal distribution.

questions.explanation: A normal distribution is symmetrical, so half the scores lie above the mean. (480 and 520 are one standard deviation from the mean; 460 and 540 are two.)

questions.title: Article analysis: a study of attention

parts.prompt: Identify the research method used in the study.

rubric.criterion: Identifies the method as an experiment.
rubric.example: The study is an experiment: the researchers manipulated a variable and randomly assigned the subjects to conditions.

parts.prompt: State the operational definition of attention.

rubric.criterion: States how the variable was measured in this study.
rubric.example: Attention was defined as the number of targets that each participant correctly detected in a ten-minute computer task.

parts.prompt: Describe the meaning of the difference between the two group averages.

rubric.criterion: Accurately describes which group scored higher or lower and what that means for the variable measured.
rubric.example: The caffeine group detected more targets. On average, the value was 46 for the group that drank caffeinated coffee and 39 for the group that drank decaffeinated coffee, and a p value of 0.01 means a difference this large is unlikely to be due to chance.

parts.prompt: Identify at least one ethical guideline applied by the researchers.

rubric.criterion: Identifies an ethical guideline that the summary shows was followed.
rubric.example: Informed consent: participants agreed to take part after being told about the study. (Also acceptable: debriefing; the right to withdraw; approval by an institutional review board.)

parts.prompt: Explain the extent to which the research findings may or may not be generalizable, using specific and relevant evidence from the study.

rubric.criterion: Explains a limit (or strength) of generalizability with reference to the sample.
rubric.example: The sample was 80 university students from one city, so the findings may not apply to people of other ages, cultures or backgrounds. Because the sample was not randomly selected from a wider population, it may not be representative.

parts.prompt: Explain how at least one of the research findings supports or refutes the researchers' hypothesis.

rubric.criterion: Uses a specific finding from the study as evidence.
rubric.example: The caffeine group detected more targets. (46 compared with 39).

rubric.criterion: Explains how the finding supports the hypothesis, using a psychological concept.
rubric.example: This supports the hypothesis that caffeine affects attention. Because subjects were randomly assigned, the difference can be attributed to caffeine. The finding illustrates caffeine is a stimulant that increases neural activity and alertness.

questions.title: Evidence-based question: Does sleep improve memory?

parts.prompt: Propose a specific and defensible claim, based in psychological science, that responds to the question.

rubric.criterion: States a claim that answers the question and can be supported by the sources.
rubric.example: Sleep improves memory because memories are consolidated during sleep.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using at least one piece of specific and relevant evidence from one of the sources. (ii) Explain how the evidence supports your claim, using a psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding learned in AP Psychology.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from one source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source A, students who slept recalled a mean of 31 of 40 word pairs, compared with 22 for students who stayed awake.

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim through memory consolidation: during sleep, the hippocampus and cortex strengthen newly encoded memories, so the sleep group stored the word pairs better. Because the study was an experiment with random assignment, sleep can be said to have caused the difference.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a psychological concept in the explanation.
rubric.example: The concept must be named and applied correctly, as in the model explanation.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using an additional piece of specific and relevant evidence from a different source. (ii) Explain how this evidence supports your claim, using a different psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from a different source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source B, participants who had more slow-wave sleep completed the maze faster the next morning (r = +0.55).

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim because NREM stage 3 sleep is linked to strengthening the neural connections formed during learning (long-term potentiation), so more deep sleep goes with better retention of the maze.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a different psychological concept from the one used in part B.
rubric.example: The concept must differ from the one used in part B and be applied correctly.
